themes.reason: Provides background scale and growth of the private rented sector, setting context but not itself explaining why fees are high or opaque.

This is the central evidentiary theme documenting what fees are charged, how much, and how they vary, directly establishing the scale and nature of the 'high, opaque' fees problem; without it there is no factual basis for the diagnosis.
Shows that despite existing transparency rules, fees remain hard to find and compare, directly supporting the 'opaque' part of the diagnosis and explaining why current safeguards are insufficient.

themes.theme: Market Failure and Lack of Competition
themes.reason: Explains the underlying cause of high and opaque fees—misaligned incentives and weak competitive pressure—forming the causal mechanism the policy argument relies on.
Documents the scale and effects of high fees on tenants' finances and mobility, establishing why the problem matters and justifying intervention.
Adds supporting examples of agent misconduct and unfair charging, reinforcing but not solely carrying the diagnosis of opacity/unfairness.
Contains unrelated or tangential remarks (e.g. discrimination against benefit claimants, Northern Ireland surveys) that do not bear directly on the core diagnosis of high, opaque fees.
